results.title: Replay of a completed step returns memoized result, body not re-run
results.claim_anchor: blog: 'the moment it succeeds, step.run records the result so it's never executed again'; 'It does not re-run'
results.notes: exec2 models server replay with memo state injected per MockedStep contract.

results.title: Commit-then-throw inside step.run: retry re-executes the step body
results.claim_anchor: blog FAQ (verbatim): 'On retry, the step body runs again, and a non-idempotent payment API will charge again'
results.expected_by_claim: their own disclosure predicts re-execution -> OBSERVED if 2 effects
results.notes: Disclosure-conformance probe: behavior matches their published FAQ window 1:1. Not a headline violation. Doc anchor added: docs 'Primitives and steps': 'A step does not make an external action exactly once. If a provider accepts a request but its response is lost, the step can retry the action.' + docs idempotency page: 'A request can succeed before Inngest records the step result.' => disclosure-conformance confirmed at docs level.

results.title: Same step ID, different payload: memo replays foreign result without conflict signal
results.claim_anchor: blog: memo is keyed by step ID only ('charge-card'); no payload binding mentioned anywhere in blog/FAQ
results.expected_by_claim: expected (claim-silent): if no binding, stale success for a different order
results.observed: exec1 (order-A) -> {"charged":true,"order":"order-A","cents":1000}; exec2 (order-B, $99.00, same id) -> result={"charged":true,"order":"order-A","cents":1000}, new executions=0
results.notes: A6-class twin (T1 p1_A6). Doc-boundary check RESOLVED 2026-10-27: docs 'Primitives and steps' (sha256 8557972...) section 'Keep step IDs stable': 'a step ID identifies work within its run; keep each logical step's ID stable' — one-ID-one-work model documented => OBSERVED (no headline violated). Sharp edge retained: no payload binding, no conflict signal on ID reuse; silent wrong-result replay in agent loops remains an unprotected hazard (hardening note, not FAIL).

results.title: Parallel branches reusing the same step ID in one run
results.claim_anchor: blog is silent; docs say IDs must be unique per run (docs-check TODO)
results.notes: Behavior record: parallel branches reusing one step ID. If both slots resolved without conflict, the SDK serializes/races silently - integrity window at SDK level.

results.title: Crash window model: checkpoint lost after provider-accept -> re-execution
results.claim_anchor: blog FAQ (verbatim): 'the charge succeeds on the payment provider's side but the step never records completion... will charge again'
results.expected_by_claim: their own disclosure predicts re-execution -> OBSERVED if 2 effects
results.observed: exec2 with empty memo: result={"charged":true,"n":2}, charges=2
results.notes: Modeled window (memo loss simulated by injection), matches their published FAQ. Full dynamic version = I5/dev-server phase.
